question: Does positive G1 concentration excess persist when the contribution of each mapped terrestrial realm is removed from the already-frozen consensus field?
scope: Descriptive geographic leverage audit of existing fields; NOT a refitted leave-one-realm-out analysis, not a new significance test, and not completion or rescue of the original strong-stability gate.

assignment.unit: the center of each original 36 x 18 equal-area grid cell
assignment.method: sample the exact frozen 0.01-degree RESOLVE integer ecoregion raster at the cell center, map its row ID through the original GPKG REALM column
assignment.unassigned: Preserve as UNASSIGNED rather than infer a terrestrial realm; include a separate fixed UNASSIGNED deletion diagnostic.
assignment.selection: all eight source realms plus UNASSIGNED; no result-dependent selection or merging

computation.base: original aggregate observed field, aggregate opportunity weights, original evaluable mask, and all 999 aggregate null fields from the primary artifact
computation.deletion: remove only evaluable grid cells assigned to the selected realm, identically for observed and every null field; retain all other original cells and weights
computation.statistic: opportunity-weighted variance, re-centering the field mean on each retained domain
computation.empty_realm: not_evaluable_no_evaluable_cells; never counted as a successful deletion
computation.p_values: none; no new inferential family or pass/fail significance label
computation.baseline_verification: reconstruct the existing full-domain concentration, ratio, and p=0.070 from the stored primary arrays before any deletion output

limitations: Deleting output-domain cells does not remove that realm's photo edges or their kernels from retained cells.
Realm assignment is at coarse grid centers; boundary-crossing cells and kernel spillover prevent literal ecological exclusion of a realm.
Unassigned cells may include ocean and coastal support; they remain a separate category, not missing values recoded to a realm.
Positive excess under all deletions is directional robustness only; the original unsupported G1 remains unsupported.
